title: Audit event guarantees and integration patterns for SIEM ecosystems
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Problem: Our current audit export paths to third-party SIEMs and aggregator endpoints (Splunk HEC, Datadog Events, custom webhooks, and partner syslog collectors) show intermittent losses and large retry storms during peak traffic. This leads to missing audit trails for tenant admin actions and noisy alerting for customers. Goals: 1) Define clear delivery semantics we can expose to customers (SLOs/SLA), 2) Standardize connector behaviors so downstream teams can reason about ordering and duplication, 3) Harden transport (auth, replay protection, schema evolution) and observability.
comments: 2026-01-18 - Design kickoff: reviewed current failures from the Jan 12 incident (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AUDIT/Jan12-Incident). Data team confirmed ~0.4% event loss under head-of-line backpressure. Action: prototype a relay with durable queue and soft DLQ.

2026-01-22 - PM feedback (Priya Patel): require per-tenant visibility (delivery_latency, last_successful_ack) and an opt-in for 'ordered-delivery' for high-compliance customers. Add cost estimate for retained events for 7 days.

2026-01-27 - Security review notes (Liam Chen): enforce mTLS for Splunk/Partner connections, rotate HEC tokens safely, add HMAC signing for webhook payloads, and document threat model. Assigned follow-up to Diego.

2026-01-31 - Implementation check-in: prototype relay writes events to persistent ledger (rocksdb) with sequence numbers, connector consumers batch to endpoints with transactional ack. Initial perf: 8k eps per core, latency median +35ms. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6123

2026-02-02 - QA plan agreed: run chaos tests (network partitions, token expiry) and a canary with 10 production tenants for 48 hours. Rollout gating: DLQ growth < 0.1% of total events and retry_rate < 2%.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable delivery semantics per-tenant: at_least_once and best_effort (exactly-once documented as not guaranteed across third-party SIEMs)
Per-tenant ordering option: monotonic sequence numbers emitted and preserved when ordered-delivery is enabled
Durable relay with short-term persistence (configurable retention, default 7 days) and a DLQ with searchable records
Authentication: mTLS or HEC token (Splunk) and webhook HMAC signing; automatic token/key rotation support documented
Observable metrics and dashboards: delivery_latency_p50/p95, retry_rate, dlq_size, connector_error_rate with tenant-scoped breakdown
Backpressure and circuit breaker behaviour: connectors stop new deliveries when downstream returns 5xx repeatedly, and surface a clear status in Console
Test coverage: integration tests for Splunk HEC, Datadog Events API, generic JSON webhooks; automated chaos and load tests included in CI
proposed_approach: Introduce an 'Audit Relay' service between the runtime event producer and connector workers. Relay responsibilities: sequencing, short durable queue, delivery policy enforcement, and per-tenant rate limits.

Delivery model: default at_least_once with idempotency tokens for receivers that support idempotent ingestion. Provide an 'ordered-delivery' flag that guarantees monotonic sequence numbers for a tenant; note downstream must accept ordering semantics.
Retries: exponential backoff with jitter and capped retry window (configurable, default 24 hours). Permanent failures go to tenant-scoped DLQ and trigger alerts.

Connector adapters: implement protocol-specific adapters for Splunk HEC (batching with HEC ACK validation), Datadog Events (bulk events API), and a generic webhook adapter with signing and backpressure response handling.

Protocol improvements: add a compact envelope with fields: tenant_id, seq_no, event_id (UUID), schema_v, timestamp, payload, hmac. Enforce schema_v in connectors and support migration via version header.
Security: require mTLS for enterprise tenants with private endpoints, otherwise fall back to HEC tokens or webhook HMAC. Log token rotation events and revoke outstanding connections on rotation.
Observability: expose tenant-level health API, and side-by-side comparison mode that duplicates events to the new relay and existing system during canary.

Rollout: gated feature flag per-tenant, stage: staging -> internal-prod -> 10% prod tenants (48h) -> ramp to 100% with health gating. Backout: disable feature flag and drain relay queue back into existing pipeline if needed.
implementation_notes: Ledger design: use an append-only local store with periodic compaction. Ensure seq_no monotonicity per tenant by sharding ledger keys by tenant_id.
Connector batching: prefer small batches (up to 512 events) to keep end-to-end latency low; allow large-batch mode for high-throughput tenants.
Ordering trade-off: ordered-delivery will sacrifice throughput (single-shard per tenant) versus default unordered which allows higher parallelism.
DLQ UX: Console should allow replay of DLQ items and an export button. DLQ items must include full raw payload + delivery_error code + last_attempt_timestamp.
Testing: build a Splunk HEC test harness that can simulate ACK delays, partial failures, and token expiry. Record metrics to the delivery dashboard for comparison.
Operational runbook: include steps to rotate tokens, evacuate relay nodes, and increase tenant rate limits safely. Add runbook to Confluence and link from Console alerts.
